findings.title: Exhausted recovery-code credential from user storage is "removed" via the local store, so it is never actually removed
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now returns the credential supplied by the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) in preference to the locally stored one. When `allCodesUsed()` is true the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only operates on Keycloak's own credential store (local DB / federated-user credential table), not on the external user storage. For a credential that lives in the user storage this either silently returns false (credential stays configured, `configuredFor()` stays true and the exhausted codes remain in the external store until the required action happens to overwrite them), or, if the provider did not populate an id on the returned `CredentialModel` (as the test provider's `createFromValues` path does), passes `null` to the JPA store and `em.find(..., null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, failing the login that just succeeded. The federated case should use `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` (or be skipped) instead of `removeStoredCredentialById`.

findings.title: Login form now parses user-storage credentials with Keycloak's internal JSON format and throws if a provider returns a plain CredentialModel
findings.body: The bean now takes the first recovery-codes credential returned by `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) and feeds it to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel()`, which `JsonSerialization.readValue`s `credentialData` and `secretData` into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`/`RecoveryAuthnCodesSecretData`, then calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()`. `getCredentials()` was introduced so providers can list their credentials in the account console; nothing in that contract requires the model to carry Keycloak's internal hashed-code JSON. A provider that returns a `CredentialModel` with only id/type/label (or with its own data format) will now cause a NullPointerException/JSON parse exception while rendering the recovery-code login page, i.e. an HTTP 500 for every user of that provider who reaches the recovery-code step, where previously only local credentials were consulted. The new format requirement is also undocumented. Either guard the federated branch (fall back to code #1 / handle parse failures) or document that providers must return a model built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`.

findings.title: Storing new codes in user storage leaves a previously stored local recovery-codes credential intact and still valid
findings.body: Before this change, recovery codes for federated users were always written via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which replaces the existing local credential of that type. Now, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true (user storage took the codes), the local credential provider is never invoked, so any recovery-codes credential already stored in Keycloak's own store for that user (e.g. created before the storage provider added support for this type, or before upgrading) is left untouched. `SubjectCredentialManager.isValid()` validates against the user storage first and then falls through to the local `CredentialInputValidator`s, so the old local codes keep authenticating the user even though they believe they regenerated them, while the login form (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`) only shows the state of the federated credential. When the user storage path succeeds, existing local credentials of type `recovery-authn-codes` should be removed as well.

findings.title: User storage only receives raw codes; userLabel and generatedAt from the credential model are dropped and the payload format is undocumented
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` hands the user storage a `UserCredentialModel("", type, <JSON array of raw codes>)`. The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction` (which carries the user-supplied label and the `generatedAt` timestamp) is only used on the local-DB branch, so a storage provider has no way to learn the label or creation time the user set (the test provider ends up with a `null` label). The shape of the challenge-response string (a JSON list of 12-char raw codes with dashes removed) is also not stated anywhere in the Javadoc, so implementers of `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential` for this type have to reverse-engineer it. Document the payload format and consider passing label/createdDate (e.g. via `UserCredentialModel` notes) so the storage can persist them.

findings.title: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without null check
findings.body: Every other credential method in this provider (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser(user)` returning `null`, but the new `getCredentials` override immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. If the credential list is requested for a user that is no longer present in the in-memory map (e.g. account/admin listing after the user was removed from the storage but a stale `UserModel` is still being used), this throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, and since `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is now called from the login form bean and the recovery-code authenticator, the NPE would surface as a 500 during login rather than a graceful fallback.

findings.title: Recovery codes stored in the test user storage can never be disabled/removed
findings.body: The provider now stores recovery codes and reports them via `isConfiguredFor`/`getCredentials`, but `disableCredentialType` only handles OTP and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` never lists `recovery-authn-codes`. Consequently admin `disableCredentialType`, the account-console delete path (which falls back to `disableCredentialType` for federated credentials), and the exhausted-codes handling in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` have no way to clear recovery codes held in this storage, and the new tests cannot (and do not) cover removal of recovery codes from user storage, unlike the existing OTP tests (`testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin`, `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage`). Add recovery codes to both methods and a test that disables them.

findings.title: Overriding getCredentials() for OTP (plus generating an OTP id) changes what the existing OTP backwards-compatibility test exercises
findings.body: This class is documented as a frozen 4.8.3-era provider used to prove old providers keep working. The PR adds `newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` and makes the new `getCredentials()` override return the OTP credential as well. `getCredentials()` is a defaulted method that an old provider would not implement, so after this change `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin` no longer exercises the legacy path where the account REST synthesizes the `otp-id` dummy credential (`CredentialHelper.createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`) and deletes it via the `-id` suffix branch; it now goes through the real federated-credential listing instead. That legacy path loses its only coverage. Keep the OTP behaviour of the provider unchanged (return only recovery codes from `getCredentials`, or add a separate provider for the new feature) so both paths remain tested.

findings.title: New test only covers the happy path of the user-storage branch
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes once and logs in once with code #0. It does not cover: (a) a federated user whose storage provider does not support `recovery-authn-codes`, which is the new fallback branch in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` that must still create the credential in the local DB (previously the only behaviour for federated users); (b) a second login to show which code number the form requests after one has been consumed, or an invalid code being rejected by the storage; (c) that regenerating codes replaces the previous set. Because the test provider's `isValid` accepts any stored code and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh model each time, the sequential/consumed-code semantics of the authenticator are effectively untested for the user-storage path. At minimum add a fallback-to-local test for a federated user and an invalid-code assertion.
